text: Research always begins with defining the problem

explanation: Defining the problem clearly is the first and most important step.

text: List the steps in the research process

text: Explain the types of research

correctAnswer: Research may be basic or applied exploratory descriptive or causal and quantitative or qualitative depending on purpose and approach.

text: State the characteristics of a good research problem
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: A good problem is clear significant researchable and feasible within time and resources.
explanation: These qualities make the problem worth studying and solvable.

text: Explain the importance of a literature review
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: A literature review avoids duplication identifies gaps refines the problem and provides a theoretical foundation and context for the study.

text: The overall plan for conducting the research is the

explanation: Research design is the blueprint for data collection and analysis.

text: In simple random sampling every member of the population has an equal chance of selection
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Random sampling gives every unit an equal and independent chance.

text: List the types of sampling methods
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Probability methods like random stratified and cluster sampling and non probability methods like convenience and judgement sampling.
explanation: Sampling methods divide into probability and non probability.

text: Explain the essentials of a good research design
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: A good design is flexible appropriate efficient and economical and minimises bias and error while answering the research question reliably.
explanation: Cover flexibility efficiency and bias reduction.

text: Data collected directly from respondents for the study is
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Primary data is gathered first hand for the current research.

text: The tool consisting of a set of questions for respondents is a
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: A questionnaire is a structured set of questions for data collection.

text: Observation is a method of collecting data by watching behaviour
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Observation records behaviour directly without questioning respondents.

text: Distinguish between primary and secondary data
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Primary data is original and collected for the study while secondary data already exists from earlier sources.
explanation: The difference lies in who collects and the original purpose.

text: Explain the methods of collecting primary data
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Primary data is collected by observation interview questionnaire and schedule each with its own strengths and limitations for different situations.
explanation: Describe each method and when it is appropriate.

text: The process of examining data to draw conclusions is
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Data analysis transforms raw data into meaningful findings.

text: The test used to determine whether sample results support the hypothesis is a
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Significance tests assess whether results could occur by chance.

text: A type one error occurs when a true null hypothesis is rejected
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Type one error rejects a null hypothesis that is actually true.

text: Define hypothesis testing
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Hypothesis testing is a statistical procedure to decide whether sample evidence supports or rejects a null hypothesis.
explanation: It accepts or rejects the null hypothesis at a significance level.

text: Explain the types of errors in hypothesis testing
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Type one error rejects a true null hypothesis while type two error accepts a false null hypothesis. Lowering one tends to raise the other for a fixed sample.
explanation: Define both errors and their trade off.

text: The final document that presents the research findings is the
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: The research report communicates the findings and conclusions.

text: Presenting another persons work as ones own is called
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Plagiarism is using others work without acknowledgement.

text: Research ethics require obtaining informed consent from participants
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Informed consent protects participants and is an ethical requirement.

text: List the characteristics of a good research report
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Clarity accuracy objectivity proper structure and appropriate presentation of data.
explanation: These qualities make the report useful and credible.

text: Explain the importance of research ethics
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Research ethics protects participants ensures honesty and integrity builds public trust and safeguards the credibility of findings.
explanation: Cover participant protection and research integrity.

text: Match the tool to its use
subject: Business Research Methods
options: Questionnaire - self administered questions|Observation - asking questions|Interview - watching behaviour|Schedule - secondary data
explanation: A questionnaire is self administered while interviews ask and observation watches.

text: Research that seeks to discover cause and effect relationships is
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Causal research tests cause and effect relationships between variables.

text: The entire group of interest to the researcher is the
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: The population is the total group from which a sample is drawn.

text: Explain the significance of research in business decisions
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Research reduces uncertainty provides evidence for decisions identifies opportunities and problems and improves the quality and success of business choices.
explanation: Cover evidence based decision making and risk reduction.

text: A variable that the researcher manipulates is an independent variable
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: The independent variable is manipulated to observe its effect on the dependent variable.

text: Explain the advantages and limitations of questionnaires
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Questionnaires are cheap cover wide areas and standardise responses but suffer from low response rates and the risk of misunderstanding questions.
explanation: Balance reach and cost against response and clarity problems.

text: Read the case: A company wants to know why its sales fell but has no clear idea of the cause. Recommend a type of research to begin with and justify it
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: The company should start with exploratory research using interviews and focus groups to understand the situation before designing a formal descriptive or causal study.
explanation: Exploratory research clarifies an unclear problem first.

text: Read the case: A researcher finds a strong association between advertising and sales in a sample. Explain what hypothesis testing would tell him and the risk of error
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Hypothesis testing determines whether the association is statistically significant or could be due to chance with the risk of type one error if the finding is actually random.
explanation: Link significance testing to the risk of false conclusions.

text: The research design that studies the same subjects over time is
subject: Business Research Methods
options: Longitudinal study|Cross sectional study|Case study|Exploratory study
explanation: Longitudinal research follows the same subjects over an extended period.

text: Explain the contents of a research report
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: A report contains the title page introduction review of literature methodology findings conclusions and recommendations followed by references and appendices.
explanation: Describe the standard structure of a research report.

text: The selection of a sample based on the researchers judgement is
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Judgement sampling is a non probability method using expert choice.

text: Explain the criteria for evaluating a research report
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: A report is evaluated on clarity of objectives soundness of method adequacy of data validity of analysis and the logic of conclusions and recommendations.
explanation: Cover each criterion for assessing quality.

text: Secondary data is generally cheaper and faster to obtain than primary data
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: Secondary data already exists so it is cheaper and quicker to collect.

text: Explain the importance of sampling in research
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Sampling makes research feasible for large populations saving time and cost and can be more accurate than a census through careful control of data collection.
explanation: Cover feasibility cost and accuracy advantages.

text: List the sources of secondary data
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Books journals government publications company records and the internet.
explanation: These published and internal sources provide secondary data.

text: Explain the steps in hypothesis testing
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Hypothesis testing proceeds from stating the null and alternative hypotheses through choosing a significance level and test statistic to comparing and deciding to accept or reject.
explanation: Trace the formal steps of a significance test.

text: A pilot study is a small scale trial run of the research instrument
subject: Business Research Methods
explanation: A pilot study tests the questionnaire on a small sample before the main study.

text: Explain the difference between exploratory and descriptive research
subject: Business Research Methods
correctAnswer: Exploratory research investigates an unclear problem to generate insights while descriptive research describes characteristics of a population or phenomenon precisely.
explanation: Contrast the purpose and flexibility of the two designs.
